what_is_priced_in.expectation: FY2026 itself is contracted rather than contested and this dive does not dispute it: the 8-K guides net sales of $13,800M to $14,200M, adjusted free cash flow of $2,400M to $2,600M, and Q3 organic growth of 34% to 36%. The disagreement is entirely about 2027 through 2030.

The street is positioned for more, not less: consensus sits at Strong Buy with a mean target near $344 and a median near $370 against a $257.08 close, with recent bank targets in a $330 to $435 range. Nobody is being talked out of this name.
what_is_priced_in.evidence: web research 2026-08-29 (aggregator summaries of sell-side targets); no filing carries a consensus figure, so this is secondary-source and is not used to set any level

priced_in_summary: TOO LATE on the COMPOUNDER clock, and the decomposition is the reason rather than the valuation being high. Over two years the price rose 219.3% while revenue per share rose 48.8%: the multiple did two thirds of the work, which is method section 7's definition of a re-rating that ate the runway. What is left in the price is a 32.95% five-year free-cash-flow CAGR. The most aggressive path this dive can defend is 19.1% revenue compounding at a 17% through-cycle free-cash-flow margin, which is 17.1% free-cash-flow compounding, and that 19% revenue number is itself an 85th-percentile outcome against the base rate that companies growing above 20% median-revert to single digits. Inverting the same solve on the same assumptions, a 17.1% implied growth rate corresponds to an enterprise value of $54.32B and a share price of $141.66, and a more generous 19% corresponds to $153.19. This is not a call that Vertiv is a bad company; it is a call that at 257.08 the market has already bought the next four years and one month of them. This becomes a dive worth re-opening below roughly $155, or on evidence that the deferred-revenue build is a permanent structural feature of the model rather than a one-cycle prepayment wave.
bull: Demand is contracted, not forecast. Deferred revenue rose $1,822.7M in H1 2026 to $3,633.7M, more than doubling in six months: customers are paying ahead of delivery, which is a harder signal than a pipeline comment. The company also reports it 'Achieved a net cash position at the end of second quarter 2026'.

Operating leverage is real and still widening. GAAP operating margin went 12.7% (FY2023) to 17.1% (FY2024) to 17.9% (FY2025) to 18.2% (H1 2026), and the company's own FY2026 guidance reconciliation implies 21.1% GAAP on midpoint revenue. Incremental operating margin over FY2023-2025 was 28.4%, well above the level being earned.

The balance sheet is a competitive weapon in a capacity race. Altman Z of 8.82 (SAFE), net cash, and $5.6B of liquidity let Vertiv fund capacity from cash flow while smaller cooling specialists cannot, and the filing says it is 'further accelerating capacity expansion and strategic investments to meet this demand and capture market share'.
bear: The free cash flow the whole valuation rests on is currently funded by customers, not by operations. H1 2026 adjusted free cash flow of $1,578.1M sits on top of a $1,822.7M deferred-revenue build; strip it and H1 free cash flow is minus $244.6M. The prior-year half had a $171.5M build on $541.5M of free cash flow, so this is new and it is a stock effect: cash keeps arriving only while the balance keeps growing.

Value capture is fragmented, not oligopolistic. Third-party market work puts Vertiv at roughly 11.3% of the data-center liquid-cooling market in 2025 with the top five holding about 35% between them, while Schneider (via Motivair) and Boyd (via Durbin) consolidate into the same space. The chain's own capture score of 50 for this link is if anything generous, and a terminal value that is 81.9% of enterprise value needs oligopoly economics it does not have.

The attention gap this machine hunts is simply absent here. 26 analysts cover it, institutions hold 84.4% of the float, PCS Axis B reads SATURATED, and the chain scores this link EMERGING rather than UNDISCOVERED. The DARK 88.2 Axis A score is a retail-chatter artifact on a $98B company, not an edge. Growth stocks bought at the 79th percentile of their own multiple with consensus at Strong Buy have a well-known problem, and it is not the business.

expectations_gap.market_implied_source: data/market/VRT.json quality.reverse_dcf [implied_fcf_cagr 0.3295, state SOLVED, base_fcf $1,893.8M, EV $98,476.1M, 9% discount rate, 2.5% terminal growth, 5-year horizon, bisection; as of 2026-08-29]
expectations_gap.solve_reproduced: The solve was re-run in session against its own stated assumptions purely as an arithmetic check and returns an enterprise value of $98.49B against the $98.48B the file carries, so the implied column is internally consistent and is quoted, never re-derived.

rows.structural_reason: Content per megawatt is rising, not just megawatts. At current accelerator densities liquid cooling and high-density power distribution are specified into a hall rather than optional, so Vertiv's revenue per unit of data-center capacity grows even where capacity growth slows. H1 2026 organic growth of 19.9% on top of FY2025's 27.8% reported growth is that effect, not a one-off.
rows.leading_indicator: EMEA organic revenue, which fell 14.8% in H1 2026 against the Americas' +31.0%. A 19% five-year path needs EMEA to stop shrinking by the FY2026 print; if the Americas is carrying the whole company, the path is regional rather than structural.
rows.note: The two columns are NOT the same unit and that is stated rather than smoothed: the data plane's solve returns a free-cash-flow CAGR of 32.95%, not a revenue CAGR. Held at the FY2026 guided free-cash-flow margin of 17.9%, 32.95% free-cash-flow compounding needs about $44B of revenue by 2030, a 33.9% revenue CAGR. Mine is 19.1% (14.0, 17.5, 20.5, 22.7, 24.5 $B for 2026-2030). Against the base rate that companies growing above 20% median-revert to single digits and only 1-3% hold 20%+ for a decade, 19% is already an 85th-percentile call, and it is barely half of what the price asks.

rows.leading_indicator: Segment adjusted operating margin: APAC ran 13.2% in H1 2026 against the Americas' 27.3%, so the consolidated number is a mix outcome. Watch whether APAC closes the gap or the group margin is simply the Americas share rising.
rows.note: Both columns are GAAP operating margin. The market column is the same cash requirement expressed as margin instead of growth: on my $24.5B of 2030 revenue, the price's $7,866M of 2030 free cash flow is a 32.1% free-cash-flow margin, translated to about 31.5% operating margin at Vertiv's own FY2025 relationship (free-cash-flow margin ran 0.6pt above operating margin). Mine holds the FY2026 guided 21.1% GAAP margin flat, which is already the top of the company's own range (12.7%, 17.1%, 17.9%, 18.2% H1 2026) and below management's stated above-27% adjusted target for 2030, roughly 24% GAAP at the current 2.7pt amortization gap.

rows.leading_indicator: Current liabilities as a share of total assets: 36.1% at FY2025 and 45.6% at 2026-06-30. Incremental returns stay top-quartile only while that ratio keeps rising, and it cannot rise forever.
rows.note: Both columns are pre-tax incremental return on invested capital (change in operating profit over change in total assets less current liabilities). The realized FY2023-2025 figure is 45.3%, and the price needs it to persist because capex is guided at only about 4.0% of revenue. It is half-funded by other people: current liabilities grew $2,102M of the $4,214M asset build over that window, so suppliers and prepaying customers financed 49.9% of the growth. Base rate: roughly 40-50% of top-quartile return firms are still there after ten years, so decay is the central case, not the bear case. Mine assumes decay to 28%.

No disagreement, and saying so matters. The solve's 2.5% perpetual growth sits at the long-run nominal GDP ceiling and is the one input this dive would not change. It is also where the money is: at the implied 32.95% growth rate, 81.9% of enterprise value sits in the terminal value beyond 2030 and only 18.1% in the five explicit years. The verdict therefore rests entirely on the five explicit years, which is the honest place for it to rest.

The price requires roughly twice the free-cash-flow compounding this dive can defend: 32.95% against 17.1% (a 15.7% to 18.3% band depending on whether the through-cycle free-cash-flow margin settles at 16%, 17% or the currently guided 17.9%). Four of the five drivers point the same way and the fifth is agreement. The gap opened through the multiple rather than through delivery, which is what makes it a TOO LATE rather than a WATCH.

independence_test.largest_disagreement: The price treats FY2026's guided step-change as a run rate; I think it is a pull-forward peak, so the market is pricing 32.95% five-year free-cash-flow compounding where I can defend 17.1%, and the difference alone is about 45% of the share price.
independence_test.why_the_gap_exists: A duration error, not a direction error, and it is the one error a bullish, well-covered consensus makes most reliably. Twenty-six analysts and a Strong Buy consensus with a mean target near $344 are all right about 2026, which is contracted; the error is extrapolating a guided year into a terminal rate. It is compounded by a cash-flow artefact almost nobody adjusts for: the $1,822.7M H1 deferred-revenue build makes reported free cash flow look like a run rate when it is a stock change, and the reverse DCF's own base is the last clean year before that distortion. Sell-side long-term forecasts run 3-5 points high as a base rate; here the required rate is 16 points above my central case.
independence_test.falsification: By 2026-11-27, this dive's review date, the Q3 2026 print will have landed against guidance of $3,650M-$3,850M net sales and 34-36% organic growth. I am wrong, and this reverts to WATCH or better, if BOTH of these appear: Q3 organic growth prints at or above 36% AND deferred revenue grows by more than $800M again sequentially from the $3,633.7M of 2026-06-30, because that would make the prepayment build a structural feature of the model rather than a one-cycle wave. I am right if organic growth decelerates toward the low 20s with deferred revenue flat or falling, which converts today's free cash flow into a working-capital headwind. The separate price trigger: below roughly $155 the same solve implies a growth rate inside my defensible band and this stops being TOO LATE.

earnings_quality.basis: Grade B: several mild flags, each disclosed and each with a defensible explanation, sitting over a clean mechanical core. Clean: Beneish M of -2.438 against the -1.78 review threshold (CLEAN, 12 of 12 inputs found); accruals of -7.3% of average assets in FY2025 (cash exceeds earnings, the conservative direction; -9.6% FY2024, -5.8% FY2023); free cash flow at 142% of net income; DSO essentially flat at 112.6, 107.6 and 110.9 days across FY2023-2025 and 115.5 annualized at H1 2026; deferred revenue rising sharply rather than draining, which delays revenue rather than pulling it forward; Altman Z of 8.82 (SAFE); Ernst & Young ratified as auditor for FY2026 at the 2026 annual meeting, no auditor change. Flags: (1) inventory days jumped from 81.6 at FY2025 to 124.8 annualized at H1 2026, which the filing explains as 'temporary supply chain congestion and multi-phased project execution as deployments scale in size and complexity'; (2) CFO turnover inside the last ten months, David Fallon (CFO since 2017) retiring and Craig Chamberlin succeeding him in November 2025, an orderly announced retirement with the predecessor retained as a consultant, not a resignation; (3) free cash flow currently funded by a $1,822.7M half-year deferred-revenue build rather than by operations, which is fully disclosed on the face of the cash-flow statement but makes the cash number a stock change; (4) the GAAP-to-adjusted gap is 19.5% at H1 2026 diluted EPS ($2.26 against $2.70) and its add-backs, intangible amortization and PurgeRite contingent consideration, recur for an active acquirer. Not A because of (1), (3) and (4). Not C because none of these is a Beneish breach, a sustained DSO or deferred-revenue drift, or an undisclosed one-time claim: everything above is on the face of the filing. Piotroski is 6 of 9 (MIDDLING), failing the current-ratio, share-count and gross-margin criteria, which is a growth-funding profile rather than a quality problem. The 8-K carries 'failure to remediate material weaknesses in our internal controls over financial reporting' in its risk-factor list; that language traces to the 2021 SPAC warrant restatement and its current remediation status could not be established from the documents on this plane, so it is recorded as an open question rather than scored either way. No related-party dealings were found; that search was not exhaustive. The veto is not load-bearing on this dive and that is stated rather than implied: grade B caps nothing, and the verdict is TOO_LATE on valuation grounds that would stand at grade A.

data_gaps: Insider activity cannot be read as a clean signal from what is on disk. The 40 filings in data/market/VRT.json insider are all grants, awards and tax withholding, with zero open-market purchases and zero open-market sales, but diagnostics.filings_listed is 450 against health.filings_examined of 40. The absence of Code S rows in an 8.9% sample is a sampling artefact, not evidence of no insider selling, and it is not used in this verdict.

quality.shares_used is 382,553,680 as of 2025-12-31, while the 8-K reports 384,936,985 shares outstanding at 2026-06-30 and 392.8M diluted shares in the FY2026 guidance reconciliation. Market cap and the reverse-DCF enterprise value are therefore struck on a share count roughly 2.6% below the guided diluted figure. Correcting for it makes the name slightly more expensive, not less, so the direction of the error favours the verdict rather than the thesis.

PCS media sub-score was not fetched (3 of 4 attention fields present) and the PCS gate state is ADVISORY because its control fixtures were unreadable in the Actions run, so Axis A is not machine-admissible evidence here regardless of what it reads.

Backlog is the single most-quoted bull fact on this name and it does not appear in the 8-K on this plane. Web summaries cite a backlog above $15B and a book-to-bill near 3x. Neither is used anywhere in this dive, because a number that load-bearing must come from a filing.

A web summary encountered during research reported FY2026 guidance of $13.5B-$14.0B revenue and adjusted EPS of $6.30-$6.40, which contradicts the 8-K on disk ($13,800M-$14,200M and $6.65-$6.75). The filing governs and the web figure was discarded. Recorded because it is a live example of why the venue rule exists.
